- **Stack-dependent suites are still outside the gate.** The build gate (`vercel.json`) covers `check`, `lint`, and the node-side Vitest project; the `client` browser project runs advisory-only in GitHub Actions. `test:e2e` and `test:integration` need a live Supabase stack and run nowhere automatically. Decide whether they earn a scheduled job — that is also the natural home for the service-drift check below.
- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (originally `003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, carried into the baseline). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path — they survive only if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback. Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert in a new migration and confirm the remote function matches.
- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That is the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was fixed by reading the year in a **`+page.ts` `load`** (`data.year`) with the arrows using **`goto`** — `load` re-runs with the right URL on every navigation. (Client-side derivation did NOT hold up: both `$app/stores` `$page` and the `$app/state` reactive `page` went stale on Back.) Apply the same `load`-based pattern here, and audit any other `$derived(… $page.url …)` site. Latent — not yet reproduced for expenses.
- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle was specced but never built. **Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.**
- **Local Supabase service versions drift silently from production.** `supabase/.temp/*-version` records the remote project's service versions **as of the last `supabase link`** and `supabase start` runs exactly those images, so local mirrors whatever prod looked like at link time. Supabase keeps upgrading the hosted project; local never moves. The pins sat at 2025-11-27 for eight months, leaving local on `gotrue v2.183.0` / `storage-api v1.31.1` against prod's `v2.193.1` / `v1.67.15` — i.e. we develop and test auth and storage, the two services `receipts` signed-URL security rests on, against versions prod stopped running long ago. `supabase start` printed the warning on every single start; nobody reads a warning in a 15-line startup log. Fixed for now by re-linking (see [Local development](local-dev.md)), but it will re-open. **Detection is scriptable:** read the four `.temp/*-version` files and diff against the `remote` field of `supabase services --output json`. Do _not_ diff against that command's `local` field — that reports the CLI's bundled defaults, not what is actually running, and yields permanent false positives. Best home is a scheduled job once CI exists; a local pre-`db:up` check would be per-developer and easy to ignore.
- **`adapter-auto` leaves the deploy target implicit.** `svelte.config.js` still uses the scaffold default, which infers the adapter from build-time env vars — on Vercel that resolves to `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel`. It works, and nothing is broken. But the choice of Node vs Edge runtime, region, and per-route function config is currently whatever the auto-detect picks, which matters for the long-running Mistral OCR calls. Pin `@sveltejs/adapter-vercel` explicitly when convenient and set the runtime deliberately. Low priority.
- **`allowScripts` is stale for `esbuild` — install scripts are being blocked.** `npm ci` warns: `esbuild@0.28.1 (postinstall: node install.js)` is not covered by the `allowScripts` map in `package.json`, which still lists only `esbuild@0.27.7`. Two esbuild copies exist in the lockfile — `0.27.7` at the root (used by Vite/Vitest, approved) and `0.28.1` nested under `tsx` (not approved). The current CI job is unaffected because `check` / `lint` / `test:quick` never invoke `tsx`, but the `seed:demo` scripts do. Either approve `esbuild@0.28.1` or confirm the nested copy works without its postinstall.
- **Watch for storage-policy drift.** `supabase db dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are hand-maintained at the end of `20260726120000_baseline.sql`. A future storage change written only as a migration will be lost the next time the baseline is regenerated; one made only in the dashboard will never reach a new environment. Consider a check that diffs live storage policies against the baseline.
- **Manually verify `ReceiptImageViewer` gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for the nothing-found-anywhere row, but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case. The tests assert the real `422`; the PRD table is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the table or leave the note.

- **Emailed receipts are never resized — the two capture paths store different things.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes straight to storage (`supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts:137`) with no size check and no resize, so a receipt forwarded by email is stored at whatever size the sender's mail client produced, while the same receipt uploaded in the browser becomes a 2400px JPEG. Deliberate for now — it is a Deno edge function with no Canvas, so matching it means a WASM image library plus a second copy of the resize rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/` kept in lock-step by hand (the burden CLAUDE.md already flags for the date-correction code), and CPU time inside a webhook that must answer quickly. Recorded as an accepted asymmetry in [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) and the ["Every uploaded image becomes JPEG" invariant](domain-model.md). Revisit if storage cost or emailed-receipt volume grows.
- **Manually verify `ReceiptImageViewer` gestures.**

Done — three docs written, no code touched.

**`docs/domain-model.md`** — two Language terms (**Source File** / **Receipt Image**) and three Invariants ("Size limits govern the Receipt Image, not the Source File", "Zoom never invents pixels", "Every uploaded image becomes JPEG"). The two terms are the ones whose absence produced the bug: `validateFile` measured one thing while the limit meant the other, and there was no word to make that visible.

**`docs/adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md`** — the decision and its rationale, with the five rejected alternatives recorded (raise the limit to 15MB, message-only, keep PNG lossless, two artifacts per receipt, 1.5× zoom headroom). The consequences section states plainly that transcoding is irreversible, that zoom disappears for small images by design, and that a resize failure now surfaces as a rejection with a different reason.

**`docs/plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md`** — implementation shape: the split validation, format handling, 2400px/85%, derived zoom ceiling, route deletion, plus the two consequential fixes (OCR gets the wrong MIME once transcoding lands; `resizeImage` decodes every file twice, which is a prerequisite for raising the ceiling, not a tidy-up). Test list and the two open questions are at the end.

**Backlog** also updated, since it's the working list: a new bug entry at the top of *Bugs / UX issues*, the email-path asymmetry under *Correctness / infrastructure* (from your "log as a known gap" answer), M2 marked slated-for-deletion, and the mobile-capture HEIC note pointed at the plan. Prettier is clean.

Two notes on what I did *not* do. I left `src/lib/version.ts` alone — per CLAUDE.md the number gets assigned at commit time, and the plan says "(pending release)" rather than a version tag. And nothing is staged; committing is yours.

The open question worth resolving before implementation is whether 2400px buys OCR anything — if Mistral downscales to ~1024–1500px internally, the extra pixels serve human zoom only. That doesn't change the decision, but it changes what the ADR should claim, and it would let a future storage squeeze cut resolution without touching OCR accuracy. Say the word and I'll build it.

1	---
2	status: accepted
3	---
4	
5	# The stored image is the contract
6	
7	## Context & decision
8	
9	`ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` validated the file the person picked and
10	_then_ shrank it. The 5MB limit therefore measured the **Source File** while the
11	resize that would have made it ~400KB ran on the next line.
12	
13	The fix is to decide what the limit is _about_. **The limit describes the
14	artifact we keep, not the artifact we are handed.** Size validation moves after
15	the resize, so it gates the **Receipt Image**; the Source File is bounded only by
16	a 25MB pre-decode ceiling that exists to protect the browser's memory, not to
17	judge the receipt. Everything follows from that principle:
18	
19	- **2400px longest axis at 85% JPEG.** The stored image is what a person zooms
20	  into, so the pixel budget is chosen for human reading, not for OCR.
21	- **HEIC and PNG transcode to JPEG.** One stored format. PNG additionally never
22	  honoured the 85% quality argument (`toBlob` ignores it for lossless formats),
23	  so a PNG "resize" could return a file _larger_ than it arrived.
24	- **Zoom stops at the image's own natural resolution**, replacing a flat
25	  `MAX_ZOOM = 400`. 100% is fit-to-viewport, so a fixed percentage meant
26	  different things per device: on a phone 400% was roughly 1:1, on a desktop it
27	  demanded ~2.3× more detail than a 2000px file contains. The mush people saw at
28	  high zoom was the viewer promising pixels the resize had already discarded.
29	- **No backfill.** A per-image ceiling reads each generation correctly on its
30	  own. Re-resizing the pre-`901b670` full-resolution originals would destroy
31	  detail we already paid to store — so `/admin/resize-images` is deleted rather
32	  than updated, which also closes the **M2** finding (an unauthenticated
33	  delete-and-reupload page) instead of deferring it a fourth time.
34	
35	## Considered options
36	
37	- **Raise `MAX_IMAGE_MB` from 5 to ~15.** A one-line unblock, rejected because
38	  the gate would still measure the wrong artifact: a 16MB photo that resizes to
39	  400KB is still refused for no reason the family can perceive.
40	- **Keep the gate, improve the error message.** Cheapest, and the honest reading
41	  of it is "we have automated shrinking, and we are going to ask you to do it
42	  anyway."
43	- **Keep PNG lossless, add a keep-the-smaller-file guard.** Genuinely defensible
44	  — JPEG ringing around small glyphs is real, and screenshot receipts have sharp
45	  edges. Rejected for a single stored format; at 2400px and 85% the artefacts are
46	  well below the threshold that matters for reading a total.
47	- **Two artifacts per receipt** — a small display/OCR copy plus a large read
48	  copy. Best quality-per-byte, rejected as doubling the storage objects and
49	  adding a second signed-URL path to every surface that shows a receipt.
50	- **Cap zoom at ~1.5× native** rather than a hard 1:1, keeping some headroom
51	  because magnification past 1:1 still helps low-vision readers even though it
52	  adds no information. Rejected in favour of the stricter rule: every pixel on
53	  screen is a real pixel.
54	
55	## Consequences
56	
57	- **Transcoding is irreversible and lossy.** Detail discarded at upload never
58	  comes back — there is no original to re-derive from, by design. Revisiting the
59	  2400px/85% numbers only affects receipts uploaded after the change.
60	- **Zoom disappears for small images.** Anything already at or below viewport
61	  size has `MIN_ZOOM == MAX_ZOOM` and both controls sit disabled. Accepted
62	  deliberately over faking magnification.
63	- **A resize failure now becomes a rejection.** `prepareFileForUpload` falls back
64	  to the original on any error; a 12MB original then fails the post-resize gate.
65	  The file is refused either way, but the real reason is "we could not shrink
66	  it", and the message must say so rather than blaming the file's size.
67	- **The email path diverges.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes
68	  straight to storage with no size check and no resize (Deno — no Canvas), so an
69	  emailed receipt is stored full-size while the same receipt uploaded in the
70	  browser becomes 2400px JPEG. Resizing there needs a WASM image library and a
71	  second copy of these rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/`, kept in lock-step
72	  by hand. Logged in the [backlog](../product-backlog.md) rather than built.
73	- **Storage now holds three generations** of Receipt Image and always will. This
74	  is fine for zoom (see the "Zoom never invents pixels" invariant) but means
75	  storage-size statistics are not comparable across upload dates.

content.content: 26	- **🔴 Phone photos are rejected by the gate that exists to shrink them — designed, not built.** `uploadAndCreate()` validates the picked file and _then_ resizes it (`ReceiptService.ts:187` → `:191`), so the 5MB limit measures the file the phone handed over rather than the ~400KB JPEG we store: a normal phone photo is refused with "Image too large. Max 5MB." one line before the code that would have fixed it. Designed in [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md) with the governing decision in [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) — move the gate after resize (25MB pre-decode memory guard), 2400px @ 85%, transcode HEIC and PNG to JPEG (fixing the skipped-HEIC bug below and PNG's never-applied compression), derive the zoom ceiling from each image's natural resolution instead of a flat 400%, delete `/admin/resize-images` (closes **M2**). No backfill needed. Also fixes a doubled decode in `resizeImage` and the wrong MIME passed to OCR.

lines: - **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.

- **Sweep the remaining `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for missing `anon` revokes.** The seed-function lockdown found that `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left a _direct_ `anon` grant in place, needing an explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`. Only `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` were fixed that way. Audit every other `SECURITY DEFINER` function for the same hole and revoke explicitly where `authenticated` is the only legitimate caller.

-- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes and re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()` — **slated for deletion**, its one-off migration job is done and re-running it would now destroy detail, see [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md); **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.

+- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.

lines: - **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.

- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account. This interacts with the unverified-alias security item below — verification is the fix, so design them together.

- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it. Designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md) (invite-by-email + `SECURITY DEFINER` accept RPC; the sanctioned membership-write path that replaces the dropped self-insert policy). The read-only half already shipped — the Profile page lists family members via the `get_family_members()` RPC — so what remains is invite / accept / remove.

-- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). Also flags a suspected bug worth verifying on-device: the receipts `accept` list includes `image/heic`, which may make iOS hand over a raw HEIC that `resizeImage()` then skips entirely (`imageResize.ts:71`), sending a full-size photo to storage and Mistral on cellular. Addressed by the HEIC→JPEG transcode in [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md), which still wants on-device confirmation of what iOS actually hands over.

+- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). One on-device check is still outstanding: HEIC is now decoded and transcoded to JPEG like everything else (see [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md)), but nobody has confirmed what an iPhone actually hands over, or that Safari decodes it as expected — if it doesn't, the resize falls back to the original and a large photo is now refused rather than silently uploaded full-size.

- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y** _(optional UX, low priority)_. A recent-categories section in the dropdown, a mobile-responsive category dropdown, and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support were specced but never built.

- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits** _(optional, low priority)_. Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (the email path never applies the vendor rule) and the read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal.

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

Two reuse findings, reported above.

Relevant files:
- `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker/src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts` (lines 11, 192, 259)
- `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker/src/lib/utils/imageZoom.ts` (line 30)
- `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker/src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts` (lines 25, 62)

Nothing else in the diff re-implements an existing shared helper — the new spec files use the canonical `fetchMock.ts` stubs and correctly avoid `supabaseMock.ts`, which its own docs exclude from `ReceiptService.*` specs.

Reviewed the diff, the three new files, and the pre-change versions for context. Findings, most impactful first. ## 1. `src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts:139` — full-resolution bitmap stays alive across the JPEG encode `bitmap.close()` sits in the `finally` (line 146), so it runs only *after* `await encodeCanvas(canvas, quality)` resolves. The bitmap is dead weight the moment `ctx.drawImage` returns (line 137). For a 12MP HEIC/JPEG that's ~48MB of RGBA held simultaneously with the 2400×1800 canvas backing store (~17MB) and the growing JPEG blob, for the whole duration of the encode — which is the longest step in the function and now runs on files up to the new 25MB `MAX_SOURCE_MB` guard. Cheaper: call `bitmap.close()` on the line right after `ctx.drawImage(...)`, and keep the `finally { bitmap.close(); }` purely as the throw-path safety net — `ImageBitmap.close()` is idempotent (a second call on a detached bitmap is a no-op), so no restructuring is needed. Peak memory during encode drops by the entire source bitmap. Everything else in the resize path is clean: every exit (unsupported type early-return, `getContext` throw, encode reject, success) releases the bitmap, and the second decode via `` + `URL.createObjectURL` is correctly gone. ## 2. `src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:244` — the retry closure pins the whole Source File just to read its name `buildReceiptInsert(file, path, extract)` receives the original `File` but uses exactly one thing from it: `sanitizeFilename(file.name)` (line 336). Because it's referenced inside the `withRetry` callback, the closure keeps the Source File (up to 25MB) reachable for the entire upload → signed-URL → OCR → insert → auto-category sequence, across up to 4 attempts with exponential backoff (~2.8s of sleeps). The resized `prepared.file` is retained in parallel. Cheaper: hoist `const originalFilename = sanitizeFilename(file.name);` above `withRetry` and pass the string into `buildReceiptInsert`. The closure then holds only the (small) prepared JPEG, and the Source File becomes collectable as soon as `prepareFileForUpload` returns. ## 3. `src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:242` — resize and the auth round trip run sequentially, and the round trip repeats per retry `uploadToStorage` opens with `await this.supabase.auth.getUser()` (line 275), which in supabase-js v2 revalidates against `/auth/v1/user` over the network. It is fully independent of the decode/encode, yet it can't start until `prepareFileForUpload` (line 237) has finished — hundreds of ms to seconds of CPU for a phone photo. It also re-runs on every retry attempt even though the user identity can't change mid-upload. Cheaper: `const [prepared, { data }] = await Promise.all([this.prepareFileForUpload(file), this.supabase.auth.getUser()]);`, then pass the user id into `uploadToStorage`. The auth latency overlaps the resize instead of stacking after it, and it's paid once instead of once per attempt. The rest of the reordering in this diff is a genuine win — moving `prepareFileForUpload` out of `withRetry` removes up to 3 redundant full decodes. ## 4. `src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts:126-139` — decode + downscale + encode all block the main thread `createImageBitmap`, `drawImage` of a multi-megapixel source, and `canvas.toBlob` all run on the UI thread, and the diff widens what lands here: HEIC now goes through the decode path instead of passing through, and the budget went from 2000px to 2400px (+44% destination pixels). With `processUploadBatch` running files strictly sequentially, a multi-photo batch is a series of main-thread stalls during which the "uploading" spinner can't paint. Cheaper: run `resizeImage` in a Worker using `OffscreenCanvas` + `convertToBlob` (`createImageBitmap` is available in workers, and `File`/`Blob` transfer to a worker without copying the bytes). Same algorithm, off the render thread. ## 5. `src/lib/components/ReceiptImageViewer.svelte:484` — opening the viewer instantiates and decodes the image twice (pre-existing) The `{#if baseWidth > 0}` / `{:else}` pair renders two *different* `` elements with the same `src`. On open, the else-branch image loads → `handleImageLoad` sets `baseWidth` → the `{#if}` swaps blocks → Svelte destroys that element and creates a fresh one → second fetch (cache hit) and second decode of the receipt, second `onload`, recomputing identical fit dimensions. Not introduced by this diff, but it's the function the diff modifies, and `handleImageLoad` now also writes `naturalWidth` there. Cheaper: a single `` with a conditional `style`/`class` expression (`style={baseWidth > 0 ? \`width:${scaledWidth}px;height:${scaledHeight}px\` : ''}`), so the element is never torn down and the image is decoded once per open. ## 6. `src/lib/components/ReceiptImageViewer.svelte:116` — forced layout on every wheel/pinch event (pre-existing) `zoomTo` calls `container.getBoundingClientRect()` plus reads `scrollLeft`/`scrollTop` on each invocation, and `handleTouchMove` calls it at touch-event rate during a pinch — each one a forced synchronous layout, interleaved with the `zoom` write that dirties layout again. Also `window.innerWidth * 0.9` is re-read inside the container's `style` derived expression (line 481) on every zoom change. Cheaper: cache the container rect on `touchstart`/`mousedown` (and on the first wheel of a gesture), invalidate it in a `resize` listener; hoist the viewport width into a `$state` updated by `` rather than reading `window` from a reactive template expression. Nothing wasteful found in the new `imageZoom.ts` (both functions are pure arithmetic, no retained state) or in the new spec files — `ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts` notably fabricates sizes via `Object.defineProperty` instead of allocating 11MB/40MB buffers, which is the right call.

| `src/lib/components/ReceiptImageViewer.svelte.spec.ts` | **Genuinely fixed.** Drives the real component; the 1:1 assertion is load-bearing. Two gaps. |
| `src/lib/services/ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts` | **Mostly real** (ordering/guard tests kill real mutations), but one test asserts its own mock, and three behaviours the diff introduces are unasserted. |

`/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker/src/lib/components/ReceiptImageViewer.svelte.spec.ts:54`

# The stored image is the contract

## Context & decision

`ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` validated the file the person picked and
_then_ shrank it. The 5MB limit therefore measured the **Source File** while the
resize that would have made it ~400KB ran on the next line.

The fix is to decide what the limit is _about_. **The limit describes the
artifact we keep, not the artifact we are handed.** Size validation moves after
the resize, so it gates the **Receipt Image**; the Source File is bounded only by
a 25MB pre-decode ceiling that exists to protect the browser's memory, not to
judge the receipt. Everything follows from that principle:

- **2400px longest axis at 85% JPEG.** The stored image is what a person zooms
  into, so the pixel budget is chosen for human reading, not for OCR.
- **HEIC and PNG transcode to JPEG.** One stored format. PNG additionally never
  honoured the 85% quality argument (`toBlob` ignores it for lossless formats),
  so a PNG "resize" could return a file _larger_ than it arrived.
- **Zoom stops at the image's own natural resolution**, replacing a flat
  `MAX_ZOOM = 400`. 100% is fit-to-viewport, so a fixed percentage meant
  different things per device: on a phone 400% was roughly 1:1, on a desktop it
  demanded ~2.3× more detail than a 2000px file contains. The mush people saw at
  high zoom was the viewer promising pixels the resize had already discarded.
- **No backfill.** A per-image ceiling reads each generation correctly on its
  own. Re-resizing the pre-`901b670` full-resolution originals would destroy
  detail we already paid to store — so `/admin/resize-images` is deleted rather
  than updated, which also closes the **M2** finding (an unauthenticated
  delete-and-reupload page) instead of deferring it a fourth time.

## Considered options

- **Raise `MAX_IMAGE_MB` from 5 to ~15.** A one-line unblock, rejected because
  the gate would still measure the wrong artifact: a 16MB photo that resizes to
  400KB is still refused for no reason the family can perceive.
- **Keep the gate, improve the error message.** Cheapest, and the honest reading
  of it is "we have automated shrinking, and we are going to ask you to do it
  anyway."
- **Keep PNG lossless, add a keep-the-smaller-file guard.** Genuinely defensible
  — JPEG ringing around small glyphs is real, and screenshot receipts have sharp
  edges. Rejected for a single stored format; at 2400px and 85% the artefacts are
  well below the threshold that matters for reading a total.
- **Two artifacts per receipt** — a small display/OCR copy plus a large read
  copy. Best quality-per-byte, rejected as doubling the storage objects and
  adding a second signed-URL path to every surface that shows a receipt.
- **Cap zoom at ~1.5× native** rather than a hard 1:1, keeping some headroom
  because magnification past 1:1 still helps low-vision readers even though it
  adds no information. Rejected in favour of the stricter rule: every pixel on
  screen is a real pixel.

## Consequences

- **Transcoding is irreversible and lossy.** Detail discarded at upload never
  comes back — there is no original to re-derive from, by design. Revisiting the
  2400px/85% numbers only affects receipts uploaded after the change.
- **Zoom disappears for small images.** Anything already at or below viewport
  size has `MIN_ZOOM == MAX_ZOOM` and both controls sit disabled. Accepted
  deliberately over faking magnification.
- **A resize failure now becomes a rejection.** `prepareFileForUpload` falls back
  to the original on any error; a 12MB original then fails the post-resize gate.
  The file is refused either way, but the real reason is "we could not shrink
  it", and the message must say so rather than blaming the file's size.
- **The email path diverges.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes
  straight to storage with no size check and no resize (Deno — no Canvas), so an
  emailed receipt is stored full-size while the same receipt uploaded in the
  browser becomes 2400px JPEG. Resizing there needs a WASM image library and a
  second copy of these rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/`, kept in lock-step
  by hand. Logged in the [backlog](../product-backlog.md) rather than built.
- **Storage now holds three generations** of Receipt Image and always will. This
  is fine for zoom (see the "Zoom never invents pixels" invariant) but means
  storage-size statistics are not comparable across upload dates.

In its favour: `processUploadBatch` (`src/lib/utils/batchUpload.ts:44`) is a
sequential `for…of await`, so a multi-file selection never holds more than one
decode at a time.

## Testing

- `imageResize.spec.ts` — dimension maths at the new 2400px threshold; HEIC and
  PNG both produce `image/jpeg`; output is never larger than the input.
- `ReceiptService` specs — a Source File over 5MB but under 25MB now succeeds
  (the reported failure, as a regression test); over 25MB is refused before
  decode; a resize failure on a large file is refused with the shrink-failure
  message; the MIME passed to OCR matches the uploaded file, not the picked one.
- `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte.spec.ts` — ceiling derived from natural size;
  controls disabled when natural ≤ viewport; top step clamps to the ceiling
  rather than overshooting.
- Manual, on-device: an iPhone upload end-to-end, plus the gesture check already
  standing in the backlog (wheel/drag/pinch after the a11y action refactor).

## Open questions

1. **Does 2400px buy OCR anything?** Mistral's vision model downscales large
   inputs internally; if its effective ceiling is ~1024–1500px on an axis, the
   extra pixels serve human zoom only. Worth confirming against Mistral's docs —
   it does not change the decision, but it changes the rationale, and it would
   let a future storage squeeze cut resolution without touching OCR accuracy.
2. **What does an iPhone actually hand over?** Still unverified on-device. The
   transcode is designed to work whether Safari offers HEIC or converts to JPEG
   itself, so this is validation rather than a blocker.

## Testing

- `imageResize.spec.ts` (node) — dimension maths at the new 2400px threshold, the
  accepted-type list, the JPEG renaming rule, and that HEIC reaches
  `createImageBitmap` with `imageOrientation: 'from-image'` rather than being
  skipped.
- `imageResize.svelte.spec.ts` (**browser**) — the function's body. The
  `.svelte.spec.ts` suffix is the only route into the Chromium project; in node
  `createImageBitmap` and `document` are both undefined, so without this file
  `resizeImage` never actually executes anywhere and transcoding is unverified.
  Asserts on the produced file: JPEG type and `.jpg` name, longest axis capped at
  2400px with the ratio preserved, a photo shrinking by more than half, and a
  transparent PNG landing on **white** rather than black.
- `ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts` — a Source File over 5MB but under
  25MB now succeeds (the reported failure, as a regression test); over 25MB is
  refused before `resizeImage` is called at all; a transcoded file over 5MB is
  still refused; a resize failure on a large file is refused with the
  shrink-failure message and on a small one falls back to the original, stored
  under its own extension and content type; the transcode lands under a `.jpg`
  key; the MIME sent to OCR matches what storage received.
- `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte.spec.ts` — ceiling derived from natural size (the
  image is never painted wider than `naturalWidth`); controls disabled when
  natural ≤ viewport; the clip box matches `VIEWPORT_FRACTION`.
- Manual, on-device: an iPhone upload end-to-end, plus the gesture check already
  standing in the backlog (wheel/drag/pinch after the a11y action refactor).

Note the browser project is advisory only — Vercel's `buildCommand` runs
`vitest run --project server` ([ADR-0005](../adr/0005-quality-gate-in-the-vercel-build-not-github-actions.md)),
so the transcode and zoom-ceiling tests gate nothing. That is the standing
trade-off, not something specific to this change.

## Known limits, deliberately left

- **The fit is computed once, at image load.** `baseWidth`/`baseHeight` come from
  the window size at the moment the receipt decodes, and nothing recomputes them
  on resize, so after resizing the window the receipt no longer fills the
  intended fraction. The 1:1 ceiling stays exact regardless (it is derived from
  the same `baseWidth` used to scale), so the "never invents pixels" invariant
  holds — only the fit goes stale. Pre-existing behaviour, unchanged here.
- **`MAX_SOURCE_MB` guards bytes, but decode cost is driven by pixels.** A
  well-compressed 3MB 12000×9000 scan still allocates ~430MB of RGBA. The same
  exposure existed under the old 5MB cap, five times smaller; a pixel-count guard
  would need the dimensions, which are only known after the decode starts.

content.text:
Commit denied — and correctly so: this project's CLAUDE.md says only humans commit. Everything is staged and ready for you.

## What changed

**The bug.** `uploadAndCreate()` validated the picked file and *then* shrank it, so the 5MB limit measured what your phone handed over rather than the ~400KB JPEG we store. Validation now runs after the resize and describes the Receipt Image; the Source File is bounded only by a 25MB pre-decode memory guard.

**Everything else per the agreed design** — 2400px @ 85%, HEIC and PNG transcoded to JPEG, zoom ceiling derived per image instead of a flat 400%, `/admin/resize-images` deleted (closes M2), no backfill.

## Three things found while building that weren't in the design

**A real bug I introduced and caught.** JPEG has no alpha channel, and the HTML spec composites an uncomposited canvas onto **black**. A transparent-background PNG e-receipt would have been stored as dark text on a black field — as the only copy. The canvas is now painted white first (`imageResize.ts:151`). The test kills the mutation.

**The transcode had zero test coverage.** `imageResize.spec.ts` runs in the node project where `createImageBitmap` and `document` are both undefined, so `resizeImage`'s body never executed anywhere — `OUTPUT_TYPE = 'image/png'` would have broken the headline feature and failed nothing. Added `imageResize.svelte.spec.ts`, which reaches Chromium via the suffix and asserts on the produced file: JPEG type, `.jpg` name, 2400px cap with ratio preserved, a photo shrinking by half, white background.

**A PNG screenshot can come out larger than it arrived.** Measured, not theoretical — JPEG spends bits on the hard edges of rendered text that PNG encodes nearly free. This is the price of the single stored format you chose over the keep-the-smaller-file guard, so I left the behaviour alone and recorded it in ADR-0006's consequences. Photographs shrink by well over half.

## One deviation from the design

The design said resize would stay inside `withRetry`. Moving validation after the resize changed that: a size rejection thrown inside the retry gets three backoff attempts, so you'd wait ~2.8s per file for a verdict that can't change. Both now sit outside; only the network steps are retried. Written up in the plan doc.

## Verification

`check` 0 errors / 0 warnings, `lint` clean, **server 1352 passed**, **client 119 passed**, production build succeeds. I mutation-checked the two load-bearing new tests (flat `maxZoom = 400`, and removing the white fill) — both fail as they should.

Worth knowing: the zoom-ceiling and transcode tests live in the `client` project, which per ADR-0005 is advisory only. Vercel's `buildCommand` runs `--project server`, so those two gate nothing.

Two things left open, both flagged in the plan: whether 2400px buys OCR anything (Mistral may downscale internally), and what an iPhone actually hands over — the HEIC path works either way, but nobody has confirmed it on-device.

`src/lib/version.ts` shows 0.62 → 0.63 in the staged set; that was your edit, not mine.

content.text:
Good question — and the answer is different for "have" and "need".

## What we have

Three real receipts, tracked in git: `resources/Sample-Reciepts/IMG_7602.png`, `7603`, `7604`.

But **no test loads them.** Their only reference is a doc comment in `src/lib/utils/receiptDateCorrection.fixtures.ts:8`, where the date-correction corpus transcribes their *printed date strings* into a data table and cites each `sourceImage` for provenance. The images are human reference material proving the vendor formats are real (Costco `YYYY/MM/DD`, No Frills `YY/MM/DD`, …); the tests run on the transcribed strings. That's a sound arrangement — it's why that corpus is fast and deterministic.

## What the new tests use

Runtime-synthesized images, no fixtures on disk: `makeImageFile()` / `makePhotoFile()` paint a canvas and hand back a `File` (`imageResize.svelte.spec.ts:19`), and the viewer spec uses SVG data URLs of an exact natural size. That's deliberate — a 3000×2000 fixture would be a megabyte in git, and the tests need to assert *dimensions and pixels*, which synthesis controls precisely and a photo doesn't.

## Where sample images would and wouldn't help

**Wouldn't:** HEIC. Chromium headless can't decode HEIC — that's the whole reason the code falls back to the original outside Safari. A HEIC fixture would fail in CI even with correct code. This stays the manual on-device check already in the backlog; no fixture fixes it.

**Would, marginally:** EXIF orientation. This is the one claim in the resize path with no behavioural test. `imageResize.spec.ts` asserts `createImageBitmap` is *called with* `{ imageOrientation: 'from-image' }`, so the regression "someone deletes the option" is caught. What isn't caught is that the option has the intended effect — and it matters, because EXIF orientation 6/8 swaps width and height, so `calculateResizeDimensions` would cap the wrong axis if it were ever mishandled. Every iPhone photo carries one.

I'd rate that a nice-to-have, not a gap: the mechanism is one browser-provided flag, and the flag's presence is pinned.

## If you want it covered

I wouldn't add a binary fixture. Better: splice a minimal APP1 EXIF segment (orientation 6) into a canvas-produced JPEG at test time — ~30 lines of byte work, nothing in git, and it tests the real decode. Assert an 8×4 source comes back 4×8.

Want me to add that? Otherwise the honest position is that the current synthetic coverage is right for this change, and the real receipts stay what they already are — provenance for the date corpus.

content.text:
Boundaries: worth testing. A real 25MB file: no.

## What's actually untested

The two comparisons are strict in a specific direction, and nothing pins either:

- `megabytes(file) > MAX_SOURCE_MB` (`ReceiptService.ts:200`) — exactly 25MB is **accepted**
- `sizeMB <= limit` (`:215`) — exactly 5MB is **accepted**

Sizes used in the spec today are 1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 11, 12, 20, 40 — nothing on either edge. Flipping `>` to `>=` or `<=` to `<` breaks no test, so the documented "Max 25MB" / "Max 5MB" contract is only enforced approximately. Two assertions at exactly 25 and exactly 5 close that, and they cost nothing — the existing `sourceFile()` helper already fabricates sizes.

## Why not a real 25MB image

**It would test the JS engine, not us.** The guard is a numeric comparison against `File.size`. `Object.defineProperty(file, 'size', …)` drives the identical branch; allocating 26 million real bytes changes nothing about which line executes.

**It would tax the gate.** The server project is what Vercel's `buildCommand` actually runs on every push. Adding a 25–40MB allocation there buys no signal.

**The thing a real file would exercise can't be asserted.** The guard's *premise* is "above this, decoding can wedge the tab." You can't write `expect(tab).not.toHaveCrashed()`, and the answer is machine-dependent — that's a characterization experiment on a real phone, not a unit test. It'd be flaky in CI.

**And the number is a proxy anyway.** 25MB of bytes isn't the real constraint; pixels are. A well-compressed 3MB 12000×9000 scan allocates ~430MB of RGBA and sails through — already recorded under "Known limits, deliberately left" in the plan doc. A byte-accurate test wouldn't validate the choice of 25.

## Recommendation

Add the two boundary assertions with fabricated sizes; skip the real file. If you want the on-device question answered, that belongs with the iPhone check already in the backlog — try a 48MP photo and see whether the decode is tolerable, then adjust the constant from evidence.

content.text:
Added four boundary cases to `ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts`:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| Source File of exactly 25MB → accepted | `>` vs `>=` on the decode guard (`ReceiptService.ts:200`) |
| Source File at 25.01MB → refused, before `resizeImage` | the edge is real, and still pre-decode |
| Receipt Image of exactly 5MB → accepted | `<=` vs `<` on the stored-image gate (`:215`) |
| PDF of exactly 10MB → accepted | the PDF branch selects a different `limit`, so it needs its own edge |

Mutation-checked both operators rather than trusting green:

- `>` → `>=` on the source guard kills **only** the exactly-25MB test.
- `<=` → `<` on the stored gate kills the exactly-5MB and exactly-10MB tests.

Each mutation is caught by precisely the test written for it, and by nothing else — which is the point. Before this, both flips passed the whole suite, so "Max 25MB" and "Max 5MB" were enforced only approximately, and the error messages could have been lying by one byte.

No real large files — the sizes are fabricated via the existing `sourceFile()` helper's `Object.defineProperty`, so the suite gains four tests and zero megabytes. Exact arithmetic, incidentally: `25 * 1024 * 1024` is an integer, so `megabytes()` returns exactly `25` with no float wobble at the edge.

Full gate: `check` 0 errors / 0 warnings, `lint` clean, **server 1356 passed** (up from 1352), **client 119 passed**.

Everything is staged, including the earlier work. The commit is still yours to make — the EXIF-orientation test from two answers ago remains un-built and un-asked-for; say the word if you want it before you commit.
